alt: Clean blue freeform pool with a light concrete deck and landscaping

problems: The bottom-right pool deck in A has brown rust-like stains. In B the deck is clean, so A changed more than the water.
The tile line along the right/bottom edge is hidden or altered by stains in A, and the tile near the steps differs from B.
The green algae water has blocky, pixelated edges where it meets the clear blue water, and the pattern looks like a digital paint-over.
Half the pool is clear blue and half is dark green. This split looks unnatural, and real algae would be spread across the whole pool.
The tree-like reflection and the floating leaves and debris look pasted on, and the leaf placement looks artificial.
The green water has a flat, plastic look with little depth or ripple texture, and it does not match the ripples in B.
The stained deck and the sharp boundary between clean and dirty water make A look like a staged edit, not a real before photo.
The dark green reflection patch looks like a sharp-edged blob. It resembles a pasted overlay more than real algae or a natural reflection of trees or a house.

The pool edge and tile line are covered or broken in places. There is a dark smudge on the bottom coping near the bottom center, and the tile line at the lower right is partly obscured by the water patch.
The leaves, twigs and green plants look randomly scattered and a little synthetic. Items such as the plant clumps near the bottom are not in image B, so they are extra objects.
The edit is not limited to the water surface. The coping at the bottom has a dark stain and chipped-looking damage that image B does not have.
The water is split into a clean blue area and a murky green area with a hard boundary. Real algae growth would be more gradual.
The tile line in the lower-left and left areas is hidden by the murky water.
